content.text: Fifty-one Chinese (Wǔshíyī diǎn / äº”å ä¸€ç‚¹) is a strategic collection game primarily played in the northern Fujian province of China. The game is centered around point-optimization within a single suit, where players attempt to assemble a hand of five cards of the same suit that totals as close to 51 points as possible. Unlike many Western card games, Fifty-one Chinese features a dynamic 'Table Exchange' mechanic where players can swap multiple cards at once with a public pool of facendup cards.
Wǔshíyī diǎn is a regional specialty of the Nanping area in Fujian. It shares a common ancestor with the Japanese game '51', but has developed more complex exchange rules and scoring nuances.
Typically 4 players playing individually. 3 players is also common.
Players draw cards from a face-down stack one by one. The starting player gets 6 cards; others get 5. The starter begins by discarding their sixth card to the table.
